faq: How long does a test take to run?
Building and checking takes a few days, and the test then runs in your store while visitors arrive. Small stores need more time. We tell you before we start how long a clear answer will likely take.
Not every store has enough visitors for a clean result. We check your traffic first and, if it is low, we suggest a simpler test or a longer window, rather than reading noise as a win.
Built in tools of your platform or recommendation app where possible, or a simple A and B app if needed. We tell you the cost of any app before use. Data stays in your accounts.
What if the test shows no difference?
That is a result too. It tells you the change is not worth keeping or paying for. We record it and suggest the next idea, so you learn something either way.
desc:
A/B testing for product recommendations shows you which suggestion placement really earns orders, instead of leaving it to opinion. Ecom Swift LLC sets up two versions, splits your traffic, tracks the result and explains it in plain words.

## What is A/B testing for product recommendations?

A/B testing for product recommendations is a controlled comparison. Half of your visitors see version A of a suggestion block, the other half see version B, and we measure which group clicks, adds to cart and orders more. Only one thing changes between the two versions, such as the position, the title or the number of items shown.

This matters because suggestion blocks are easy to add and hard to judge. A block that looks good in the editor can sit below the fold, push the buy button down on a phone or repeat items the shopper already owns. Without a test, you only learn about these problems by watching revenue drift.

## How testing changes what you decide

A test replaces a debate with evidence from your own shoppers. Two people on your team may disagree about whether suggestions belong above or below the product description. A split test answers that question using real clicks, add to cart events and orders on your own store.

The mechanism is simple. Because both versions run at the same time, season, ads and promotions affect both groups equally. Any difference that remains can be linked to the change you made. That is why a before and after comparison is weaker: something else always changed in the meantime.

Testing also protects you from bad ideas. A change that feels clever can lower orders, and you will see that early and can switch it off. Read the result with care, because small traffic can produce noisy numbers, and the outcome also depends on your products and visitors.

## What a good test program includes

- One clear question per test, written before anything is built.
- A single changed element, so the cause of any difference is obvious.
- A fair traffic split that we check for balance.
- Tracking for clicks on suggestions, add to carts and completed orders.
- A written goal, a time limit and a rule for how much data is enough.
- Separate views of new and returning visitors where the package includes it.
- A plain written summary: what happened, how sure we are and what to do next.
- Notes on what the test taught you, so later tests start smarter.
- A short list of follow up ideas, ordered by likely value.

## How we run your tests

We start by choosing the placement to test, such as the product page, the cart or the home page. We then agree the question, the metric that decides the winner and the stopping rule. Setting the rule first stops anyone from calling a winner early because a number looks good on day two.

Next we build both versions in your store or your recommendation tool, check that the traffic split is balanced and confirm that tracking fires on every version. We watch the first sessions to make sure nothing breaks on phones or in checkout. When the test ends, we read the results and send you the summary.

The Basic package covers one test on one placement. Standard adds a second test and a written plan. Premium runs tests in a planned order, adds new versus returning segments and gives you a roadmap and a results call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Test one change at a time.
- Decide the winning metric before the test begins.
- Let the test run for the full agreed time.
- Check results on phones and desktop separately when traffic allows.
- Write down what you learned, even when there is no winner.

**Avoid:**
- Stopping the moment one version looks ahead.
- Running a test during an unusual sale unless you test the sale itself.
- Changing the design halfway through.
- Testing several placements in the same test.
- Treating a flat result as a failure, because it tells you where not to spend time.

## Who this is for

This service suits store owners who already show suggestions and want proof of what works. It also suits teams about to redesign a product page who want to compare the old and new block before committing. A smaller store with modest traffic can still benefit, as long as we pick a test that is bold enough to show a visible difference.

## What we need from you

Tell us which placement worries you most and what you would like to learn. Share the name of your recommendation tool or theme and a rough idea of your monthly visits. Give us access as a collaborator, staff or developer user where your platform supports it, and never send a password. We confirm the plan before we change anything.
